title: AI-driven dynamic psychological measurement: correcting university student mental health scales using daily behavioral and cognitive data.
summary: LLM/RAG-based score adjustment used daily behavioral and cognitive data from 177 university students. The paper reports higher AUCs than standard scales for anxiety and depression classifications and longitudinal decreases on clinician-rated scales, while SCL-90 specificity worsened; these observational measurements do not show intervention efficacy or diagnostic validity.
ai_technology: Large language models with retrieval-augmented generation dynamically adjust questionnaire scores using daily behavioral and cognitive data.
organization: Inner Mongolia People’s Hospital; Inner Mongolia Medical University

evidence.tested: Among 177 students, reported AUC was 0.95 versus 0.86 for anxiety and 0.93 versus 0.82 for depression; HAM-A/HAM-D scores declined while SCL-90 specificity worsened.
evidence.unknown: Longitudinal observational comparison; score changes do not demonstrate an intervention effect, clinical diagnosis, or generalizable measurement validity.
evidence.ai_role: LLM/RAG score adjustment is linked to differences in scale-based assessment and longitudinal score patterns.

source_review.scope: Primary source full-text Methods and Results; version date and reported validation scope checked.
